# zumen

> AI-editable diagrams as code. A diagram tool whose source of truth is text (one YAML file),
> built so that **a human's edit survives the next AI pass**. Desktop app (Tauri), MIT licence,
> with an MCP server so an agent (Claude Code and others) can read the spec and write drawings.
> Renders SVG; exports Mermaid and draw.io.

This file is for AI assistants and agents reading the site. It is written and
kept in the repository (`site/llms.txt`); the counts in it are stamped by
`pnpm gallery`, so they cannot drift from the examples.

Note: this is a GitHub Pages project site, so this file is served at
`/zumen/llms.txt` rather than at the domain root.

## The claim, in one line

Ask in prose, a drawing appears, a human fixes one thing, ask again, and the
human's fix is still there. Measured over 10 real AI round trips: 10/10 kept
every human edit, and a human pin survives regeneration in 163/163 of the
example drawings.

How: what a person pins lives in a `pins:` block that the AI is not allowed to
write. Regeneration rewrites `nodes:` and `edges:` and cannot touch `pins:`.

## What it is

- Example drawings: 423 (all generated from the YAML in `examples/gallery/`)
- Source of truth: one `.zumen.yaml` file, readable and writable by hand
- Output: SVG (light and dark), Mermaid, draw.io XML, Markdown embedding
- Print: name the paper (`paper: B4`, A3–A5, B4/B5, Letter, Legal, Tabloid, portrait or landscape) and the SVG comes out at real size in mm; 1 px is a 96 dpi pixel, so build inside the printable area (895 × 1300 px on B4 portrait). `pnpm pdf` and the MCP export write a PDF of that sheet; the app shows the paper frame and a print preview
- Validator: 75 checks that say, in the writer's terms, what will not be drawn
- Desktop GUI: Tauri, deliberately limited to eight operations
- Agent interface: an MCP server (`zumen_inspect`, `zumen_timelapse`, and others)
- Licence: MIT

## What it is not

- Not a web app, and there is no real-time collaboration
- Not a rich editor: the GUI exists to approve or reject what the AI changed
- Not an importer of other formats
- Past about 30 nodes the text is too small to read even printed on A3, and the
  tool says so (`tooTangled`, `tooSmallToPrint`) rather than pretending otherwise
- Ribbon-like strokes (taping charts, knot charts) do not draw yet

## Range of the examples

Not only boxes and arrows. Among the 423: floor plans with grid lines and
dimensions, wall sections, transit maps and train graphs, periodontal charts,
stage lighting plots, container ship bay plans, fishing rigs, a metes and bounds
plat, a lane closure plan (MUTCD), a wildland fire IAP map, a marching band
drill chart, a weaving draft, a cabin layout (LOPA), residential ductwork.

One rendering model and a small set of primitives, not a per-industry engine.

## Every drawing has its own page

Each example has a stable URL by number, and each field has a page listing its
drawings. The per-drawing page carries the drawing itself, one line saying what
it answers, and **the rules written in its source** — the part that exists
nowhere else. The source YAML is linked from there.

- `https://meta-taro.github.io/zumen/g/<number>/` — one drawing (Japanese)
- `https://meta-taro.github.io/zumen/en/g/<number>/` — one drawing (English)
- `https://meta-taro.github.io/zumen/c/<field>/` — one field (Japanese)
- `https://meta-taro.github.io/zumen/en/c/<field>/` — one field (English)

Fields:

- `tetsudo` — Transit and transport (21)
- `kenchiku` — Building and civil (57)
- `bosai` — Disaster and emergency (20)
- `manabi` — Learning and geometry (10)
- `ongaku` — Instruments and acoustics (4)
- `setsubi` — Services and electrical (14)
- `iryo` — Health, food and farming (23)
- `tenpo` — Retail and logistics (17)
- `gyomu` — Work and organisations (25)
- `moyooshi` — Events and games (25)
- `ui` — UI and screen design (7)
- `it` — IT and software (10)

The full list of URLs is in `https://meta-taro.github.io/zumen/sitemap.xml`.
